**What is a Data Lakehouse?**

A **data lakehouse** is a modern data management architecture that combines elements of both **data warehouses** and **data lakes**. Its goal is to provide the reliability, performance, and structure of a data warehouse, while also offering the scalable, low-cost storage and flexibility of a data lake.

**Key Points:**
- **Stores structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data** like a data lake.
- **Supports SQL queries and BI workloads** like a data warehouse.
- Utilizes newer technologies (e.g., Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi).
- Makes it easier to do machine learning, real-time analytics, and business intelligence all in one place.

**How is it Different from a Data Warehouse?**

| Aspect                 | Data Warehouse                    | Data Lakehouse                           |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| **Data Types**         | Structured (tables, columns)      | Structured, semi-structured, unstructured|
| **Storage Cost**       | Higher (proprietary formats)      | Lower (cheap cloud object stores)        |
| **Flexibility**        | Fixed schema (schema-on-write)    | Flexible schema (schema-on-read/write)   |
| **Data Processing**    | Mainly SQL, OLAP                  | SQL, ML, Streaming, OLAP & unstructured  |
| **Performance**        | High for SQL, BI                  | High for SQL, BI, ML with new formats    |
| **Use Cases**          | Business intelligence, Reporting  | BI, ML, Streaming, Data Science, Analytics|
| **Technology Example** | Snowflake, Teradata, BigQuery     | Databricks Lakehouse, Delta Lake, AWS Glue/Athena + Iceberg |

**Summary of Differences:**
- **Data Lakehouse** supports a wider range of data and analytic workloads compared to a **Data Warehouse**.
- Data lakehouses offer better flexibility and can support fast evolving data needs (streaming data, ML), while warehouses are best for structured, stable reporting.
- **Lakehouse** technologies add missing features (transaction support, ACID compliance, governed data management) to data lakes—making them warehouse-like for analytics.

**In essence:**
- Data Warehouses = Best for traditional BI over clean, structured data.
- Data Lakehouses = Blend the best of both for modern, all-in-one analytics platforms.

---

**References for Further Reading:**
- [Databricks: What is a Lakehouse?](https://www.databricks.com/data-lakehouse)
- [AWS: Data lake vs. data warehouse vs. data lakehouse](https://aws.amazon.com/big-data/datalakes-and-analytics/what-is-a-data-lakehouse/)
